key_insight: Citizen-led PV remains viable under declining electricity prices mainly when users coordinate sharing and governance, not when they rely on storage or subsidies alone.
engineering_relevance: For distributed PV design, the highest-leverage decisions are allocation rules, self-consumption coordination, and market-aware sizing rather than adding hardware complexity.
method: Analyzed high-resolution consumption data from a rural 24-user community sharing one PV installation
Compared static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing schemes
Evaluated scenarios with and without battery storage under current pricing and surplus-remuneration rules
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that collective self-consumption lowers required PV capacity and investment cost while increasing annual savings versus individual operation, but battery value is limited under current market conditions.
watch_item: Fairer or more flexible sharing schemes can add governance complexity, so operational simplicity may trade off against efficiency gains.
paper_title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation
